description: Serves the SPA HTML. Embeds window.YT (cluster configs, parameters.login, parameters.version) and window.__DATA__ (settings, ytApiUseCORS, uiSettings, allowPasswordAuth, ...) as inline scripts. Cluster list is NOT fetched by the client; it comes from here.

response.body_schema: text/html; inline script sets window.YT = {clusters: {...}, parameters: {version, login, authWay}} and window.__DATA__ = {settings:{data,meta}, ytApiUseCORS, uiSettings, odinPageEnabled, allowPasswordAuth, ...}

description: Bootstrap step 1. Server-side calls GET <proxy>/auth/whoami and GET <proxy>/version in parallel. A missing/failed version blocks the whole app (PRELOAD_ERROR.CONNECTION); a missing csrf_token blocks it with PRELOAD_ERROR.AUTHENTICATION. The client stores csrf_token in the cookie ytfront_<cluster>_xsrf_token.

response.body_schema: {token?: {login: string, csrf_token: string}, version?: string, tokenError?: YTError, versionError?: YTError}

description: Bootstrap step 2 (cached server-side). Server issues two execute_batch calls to the cluster proxy: (1) list //sys/primary_masters; (2) list //sys/media, get //sys/scheduler/orchid/service/version, get //sys/@ui_config, get //sys/@ui_config_dev_overrides, get //sys/primary_masters/<first>/orchid/service/version. All sub-requests carry suppress_transaction_coordinator_sync:true and suppress_upstream_sync:true. Only mediumList errors are fatal client-side.

response.body_schema: {mediumList: BatchResultsItem<string[]>, schedulerVersion: BatchResultsItem<string>, masterVersion: BatchResultsItem<string>, uiConfig: BatchResultsItem<object>, uiDevConfig: BatchResultsItem<object>} where BatchResultsItem = {output?: any, error?: YTError}

description: Root page (/) only: version of every configured cluster, via GET <proxy>/version per cluster.
Root page (/) only. When allowPasswordAuth is off, every cluster is reported authorized:true.

User settings, backed by a Cypress document under userSettingsConfig.mapNodePath. Preceded by POST (create, ignore_existing). Only active when userSettingsConfig is configured; all errors are swallowed client-side.

The single reverse proxy the browser uses for ALL YT commands when ytApiUseCORS is falsy (the default). Validates version/command against the javascript-wrapper command list; resolves a heavy proxy via GET <proxy>/hosts for heavy commands (read_table!) unless isLocalCluster or disableHeavyProxies; forwards query string, body and all headers except host/cookie, adding accept-encoding:gzip, X-YT-Correlation-Id, X-YT-Suppress-Redirect:1 and Cookie: YTCypressCookie=<secret>. The response is streamed back verbatim, so all X-YT-* response headers survive.

response.body_schema: streamed verbatim from the cluster proxy

description: Only fired when the table URL carries columns=<hash>. Returns a saved column selection.

Password login. Proxies to POST <proxy>/login with Authorization: Basic base64(user:pass); duplicates the YTCypressCookie Set-Cookie header as <cluster>_YTCypressCookie. Only needed when allowPasswordAuth is enabled.

response.body_schema: streamed from the cluster proxy; Set-Cookie: YTCypressCookie=... and <cluster>_YTCypressCookie=...

description: Plain-text cluster version. Called by the UI Node server from /api/cluster-info and /api/clusters/versions. A failure here blocks the whole UI.

Returns the authenticated login and a CSRF token. Called by the UI Node server from /api/cluster-info. The csrf_token becomes the ytfront_<cluster>_xsrf_token cookie and is echoed as X-Csrf-Token on subsequent authenticated requests.

Heavy-proxy discovery. Called by the UI Node server before forwarding heavy commands (read_table) unless the cluster is local or disableHeavyProxies is set; res.data[0] becomes the target host. The browser never calls it (useHeavyProxy is false client-side).
Returns the supported API versions. Not used by the UI; useful for smoke-testing a mock.

Cypress read. Parameters travel in the JSON body (useBodyForParameters). Path suffixes the UI uses: /@ (all attributes), /@<attr>, &/@<attr> (link suppression), #<object-id>/@<attr>. Unrecognized parameters are kept and forwarded by the driver. v3 returns the value unwrapped.

params.attributes: optional list<string>; DEFAULT = universal filter (all attributes)
params.output_format: optional; the UI passes {$value:'json',$attributes:{stringify:true,annotate_with_types:true}} on the batch envelope

response.body_schema: v3: the node value directly (JSON with $attributes/$value on demand). v4: {"value": <same>}

description: Directory listing for the navigation map_node view. NB the driver default for `attributes` is an EMPTY filter (unlike get, whose default is the universal filter). With attributes non-empty each entry is a string node carrying $attributes.

The workhorse of navigation. Sub-requests always run with an internal YSON output_format, so the batch's own output_format governs only the outer envelope. Commands with Tabular/Binary output (read_table) are REJECTED inside a batch. Each result element is {} | {output: ...} | {error: {...}}.

params.requests: required Array<{command: string, parameters: object, input?: any}>
params.output_format: the UI sends {$value:'json',$attributes:{stringify:true,annotate_with_types:true}} for the navigation attributes batch

Everything the navigation header, the table meta panel and the schema tab render comes from here; there is NO separate get //path/@schema or @row_count call. Row count is derived from chunk_row_count (row_count is NOT requested).

description: Fired from updateView to decide whether to start tablet-error polling. Two get sub-requests: <path>/@type and <path>/@dynamic. Only when dynamic is true AND type is table|replication_log_table does further polling happen, so a mock returning dynamic:false ends the chain.
Fired from updateView for every node. Error code 500 (NODE_DOES_NOT_EXIST) is explicitly tolerated, so a mock may always answer with that error.
Description block on the navigation content tab: get <path>/@ with attributes [annotation, annotation_path].

Fired from updateView only when the node has an `account` attribute. Two sub-requests: write on <path> and use on //sys/accounts/<account>. Result drives isWriteable / isAccountUsable; failures degrade gracefully.
Bootstrap: is the current user in the `admins` group (isDeveloper flag)? Errors are caught and turned into false, so a mock may answer with an error element.
On-demand only (the map-node 'recursive usage' content mode). Chunks of up to 200 get sub-requests, path form '<node>&/@recursive_resource_usage' with timeout 60000.

The static-table viewer. ALWAYS /api/v3 even via yt.v4 (the command config pins version:'v3'). Heavy (the UI Node server resolves a heavy proxy via /hosts). Parameters are the JSON POST body. The row range is a YPath STRING suffix '<path>[#lower:#upper]', not a ranges object (the object form with lower_limit/upper_limit tablet_index+row_index is used only for the unmounted-unsorted dynamic-table fallback). Two calls per table open: (1) column-discovery preload with column_names:[] and range [#0:#0] for a strict schema, (2) the real page with the selected columns. requestedPageSize = pageSize + 1 (one extra row detects end-of-table).

params.control_attributes: not sent by the UI; driver defaults

response.body_schema: Content-Type: application/json. Body = web_json: {"rows": [{col: {"$type":..,"$value":..} | [val, "typeIdx"]}], "incomplete_columns": "false", "incomplete_all_column_names": "false", "all_column_names": [sorted strings], "yql_type_registry"?: [...]}. Header X-YT-Response-Parameters: {"approximate_row_count": i64, "omitted_inaccessible_columns": [], "start_row_index"?: i64}. On error with dump_error_into_response the pretty JSON error is APPENDED to the body between two 80-'=' delimiter lines.

description: Polled every 600 s by SupportedFeaturesUpdater. Parameters would be in X-YT-Parameters headers (GET), but the UI sends an empty object. Failure is non-fatal.
Standalone (non-batch) call from the table meta panel: {path, transaction_id, permission: 'full_read', user}. Degrades gracefully on failure.
The only v4 call on the table path: get <path>/@has_row_level_ace from the table meta panel. Response is wrapped as {"value": ...}. Degrades gracefully on failure.
NOT USED by the UI (no call site in src/ui). Documented for completeness. Heavy. Output is a bare list (ProduceOutput, so no v4 wrapping).

response.body_schema: Array<{column_data_weights: Record<col,i64>, legacy_chunks_data_weight: i64, timestamp_total_weight?: i64, column_min_values?: ..., column_max_values?: ..., column_non_null_value_counts?: ..., column_estimated_unique_counts?: ..., chunk_row_count?: i64, legacy_chunk_row_count?: i64, read_size_estimate?: i64}>

description: Only relevant when ytApiUseCORS is true (browser talks to the cluster proxy directly). Handled before the API handler: if Origin is allowed, replies 200 with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials:true, Access-Control-Allow-Origin:<echoed Origin>, Access-Control-Allow-Methods:'POST, PUT, GET, OPTIONS', Access-Control-Max-Age:3600 and Access-Control-Allow-Headers:<31-entry whitelist>. Non-OPTIONS responses instead carry Access-Control-Expose-Headers with the same whitelist. Allowlist defaults: host_allow_list=["localhost"], host_suffix_allow_list=[".yandex-team.ru"], disable_cors_check=false.

Optional response chunk-framing. Enabled purely by the PRESENCE of the X-YT-Accept-Framing request header (value ignored) plus api/framing/enable (default true); signalled back with X-YT-Framing: 1. Wire format: Data frame = 0x01 + ui32 little-endian length + payload (zero-length legal); KeepAlive frame = the single byte 0x02 with no length and no payload. Framing is OUTSIDE compression: frame(compress(data)). Keep-alives start only after the driver emits response parameters, period api/framing/keep_alive_period (default 5 s). The UI/javascript-wrapper NEVER sends X-YT-Accept-Framing, so a mock can ignore this entirely.

response.body_schema: octet stream of frames; response header X-YT-Framing: 1

description: Error contract. Pre-flush: status 400 for EVERY error unless an earlier stage set 401/403/404/415/503; body is the JSON error; headers X-YT-Error (JSON), X-YT-Error-Content-Type, X-YT-Response-Code, X-YT-Response-Message. Post-flush (streaming): status stays 200, the partial body is kept and the same four fields are emitted as HTTP TRAILERS (advertised via 'Trailer: X-YT-Error, X-YT-Response-Code, X-YT-Response-Message' unless X-YT-Omit-Trailers). With the parameter dump_error_into_response:true the pretty JSON error is appended INTO the body between two 80-'=' delimiter lines — this is what the UI parses for read_table.

How the proxy assembles command parameters, in increasing precedence: (1) {input_format, output_format} inferred from headers; (2) the query string (i64-looking values become integers; a[b][0][] nesting up to depth 6; a top-level {$value,$attributes} map is unwrapped); (3) X-YT-Parameters verbatim, OR the concatenation of X-YT-Parameters0/1/... or X-YT-Parameters-0/-1/... which is then BASE64-DECODED; (4) the JSON POST body (only when the method is POST and the body is non-empty). The header format for (3) comes from X-YT-Header-Format (default 'json'; the UI sends '<encode_utf8=%false>json'). X-YT-Header-Format itself has NO multi-part support.

Output format precedence: (1) if OutputType is Null or Binary the format is forced to yson regardless of headers; (2) X-YT-Output-Format header; (3) exact-match on the Accept MIME (application/json -> json; no q= weights, no wildcards); (4) default by data type: Structured -> json, Tabular -> <format=text>yson, Null/Binary -> yson. The output_format command PARAMETER (body/query/X-YT-Parameters) overrides all of this because it is patched on top. Response Content-Type comes from FormatToMime: Json and WebJson both map to application/json.

A control-role proxy redirects heavy commands with 307 Temporary Redirect to Location '<scheme>://<data-proxy>:<request-port><path>?<rawQuery>' plus Connection: close. Suppressed by the PRESENCE of X-YT-Suppress-Redirect (value ignored), by a Cookie header (treated as a browser request), or when the proxy role is not 'control'. write_table (Tabular input) can never be redirected and gets 503 instead. The UI sets useHeavyProxy:false so the browser always sends X-YT-Suppress-Redirect:1, and the UI Node server adds it too — a mock never needs to redirect.

response.body_schema: 307 with Location header, or 503 'There are no data proxies available' + Retry-After: 60
